title: Choose the visual world for CoolVest
question: This is the direction for the CoolVest sales site. Keep it, adopt an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Cold Chain
options.lineage: Cold-chain shipping labels, ISO 780 handling pictograms and temperature-logger strip charts
options.thesis: Treat CoolVest as a cold-chain object: charge it cold, carry it, swap it at midday. The whole site reads like the label, the logger and the handling sheet.
options.viewport: A big ruled shipping label as the hero: CoolVest, 'Keep below 28 °C', handling pictograms, and a logger strip printing a shift's temperature line. A 'Request a quote' action sits in the label's address block.
options.risk: It could look like pharmaceutical packaging if the worker never appears. The guard photo and the uniform have to carry the human side.

raised.raise: The layer stack scrolls as six physical planes: the uniform lifts away to show the shirt, then the liner, then the mesh.
Two-ink discipline: logger ink plus one signal colour, never a scatter of accents.
States print themselves: the 28 °C logger line draws as you scroll, and form status prints as label lines.

options.label: Heatwave Bulletin
options.lineage: IMD heat-wave warning maps and colour-coded yellow, orange and red alert bulletins
options.thesis: The site opens as today's heat-alert bulletin for India and the Gulf, then CoolVest answers it with a system for employers.
options.viewport: A full-bleed alert map in orange and red with the bulletin headline, and the CoolVest system answering in a ruled panel beside it.
options.risk: It's the more familiar choice: heat-themed oranges are where many cooling brands land, and fear-led framing can read as alarmist.

options.label: Multiplane Layers
options.thesis: The garment is literally layers, so the site becomes a camera sinking through uniform, shirt, liner and mesh.
options.viewport: A full-bleed uniformed worker, with planes peeling back on scroll to show each layer.
options.case: Strongest on product clarity: it shows 'invisible under the uniform'. It's weaker on audience: painterly gouache doesn't speak to procurement.
options.risk: Heavy on assets. Without real painted plates it turns into generic parallax.

options.label: Noir One-Sheet
options.thesis: A guard small at noon, with the heat cast as a huge hard shadow.
options.viewport: A small figure, a huge shadow and a condensed title.
options.case: Dramatic, but buyers don't recognise themselves in a film poster.

options.label: Phosphor Terminal
options.thesis: The product as a printed transcript.
options.case: Loses on both: a garment isn't software.

options.label: Punk Paste-up
options.kept: Labels slap down, they don't fade in.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean product site in the style of Ergodyne or Techniche, executed with full craft.
canonCard.viewport: A product photo, a headline, feature icons and a quote button.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every cooling-vest brand by design.
